name: claudeignore-guard
description: Makes `.claudeignore` actually work. Claude Code has no native .claudeignore (anthropics/claude-code#579, #4160, #29455) yet blog posts teach it as if it did, so people list .env there and believe they are protected while nothing reads the file. This PreToolUse hook enforces it: Read/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit on a path matched by a .claudeignore is denied, and the denial names the exact file and line of the rule that blocked it. Matching is git's own — each .claudeignore is mirrored into a scratch tree as .gitignore and queried with `git check-ignore`, so gitignore semantics (negation, anchoring, **, dir-only rules, nested files, precedence) are exact rather than re-implemented, and paths that do not exist yet are still answered. Querying the project directly would fold in its real .gitignore and block every build artifact too. Does NOT cover Bash or Grep/Glob (see docs); permissions.deny remains the real security boundary. Requires git. Env: CLAUDEIGNORE_DISABLED=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_MODE=warn.
